mainTopic: What holds up the earth, and ריש לקיש's seven heavens and what each one contains.
overview: The גמרא keeps reading the first פסוקים of בראשית. It explains that the word 'את' shows שמים came before ארץ. A parable about a king and his early-rising servants explains why the earth gets special attention. Next comes a ברייתא of רבי יוסי about what holds up the earth, a chain that ends with God's arm. Then other opinions say the earth rests on twelve pillars, on seven, or on one pillar, the צדיק. רב יהודה says there are two רקיעים, but ריש לקיש counts seven and describes each one: וילון, רקיע, שחקים, זבול, מעון, מכון and ערבות. Each heaven gets a פסוק showing it is called שמים. Along the way come teachings about learning תורה at night, a challenge about harmful weather that דוד prayed to bring down to earth, and a list of the treasures, souls and angels in ערבות. The amud ends with a question about whether darkness can surround ה׳, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק need the word 'את הארץ'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the first פסוק needs the word 'את' before 'הארץ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the words 'and the earth' (with the extra word 'את')?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing its word-by-word reading of the first פסוק in בראשית. It asks what the extra word 'את' before 'הארץ' teaches us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes that no word in the תורה is extra. Since the פסוק could have just said 'the heavens and the earth', the word 'את' must be teaching something. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? This is the standard way to ask what an extra word teaches.
A small Hebrew word that points to the object of a verb; the גמרא treats it as a hint.

phrases.english: Why do I need 'and the earth' (et ha'aretz)?
phrases.notes: From בראשית 1:1. The question is about the small word 'אֵת' that comes before 'הָאָרֶץ'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (before this section) of the words in the first פסוק of בראשית.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the seemingly extra word 'את' before 'הארץ' teach?

steps.title: Heaven came before earth
steps.stepSummary: The word 'את' teaches that שמים were created before ארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches that heaven came before earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the wording of the פסוק shows that heaven was created first and the earth came after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'את' we might think heaven and earth were made at the same moment. On that reading, they are listed one after the other only because two names cannot be said at once. The extra 'את' shows that the order is real. The heavens come first in the order of creation.

keyTerms.meaning: To put first, to make come before

phrases.english: To teach that heaven came before earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'את' shows that שמים came before ארץ in the order of creation.

steps.title: Why does the second פסוק talk about the earth first?
steps.stepSummary: The first פסוק started with the heavens, so why does the second פסוק go straight to describing the earth?
steps.simpleTranslation: The next פסוק says: 'And the earth was unformed and void.' Since the תורה began with heaven first, why does it now describe the making of the earth first?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second פסוק and points out something odd. It asks why the תורה now talks about the earth before saying anything more about heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that heaven came first. So we would expect the next פסוק to keep talking about heaven. Instead, it describes the earth, and the גמרא wants to know why the earth gets this attention.

keyTerms.meaning: After all, since (it is already known that)
What is different? Why the change?

phrases.english: 'And the earth was unformed and void.'
After all, it began with heaven first;

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא דְּקָא חָשֵׁיב מַעֲשֵׂה אֶרֶץ?
phrases.english: what is different that it now describes the making of the earth?

steps.triggerLanguage: מכדי בשמים אתחיל ברישא מאי שנא דקא חשיב מעשה ארץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 2. If heaven comes first, why does the second פסוק turn to the earth?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the second פסוק describe the earth instead of continuing with heaven?

steps.title: The parable of the king and the early risers
steps.stepSummary: A king praises the servants who are not used to rising early but came early anyway. In the same way, the earth gets special mention.
steps.simpleTranslation: A teacher from the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: This is like a human king who told his servants, 'Come early to my door.' He got up and found women and men there. Whom does he praise? The ones who are not used to getting up early, yet did.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a parable. The one who makes an unexpected effort deserves special praise, so the earth gets special attention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the parable, the women are the ones not used to rising early, so they get the extra praise. The earth is low and physical, and we would not expect it to be created together with heaven. So the תורה praises it by describing it at more length.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher from the study house of רבי ישמעאל taught
Flesh and blood; a human (not God)

steps.whatToRemember: The earth gets attention in the second פסוק as a kind of praise. Like the servants who came early when no one expected it, the earth was created together with heaven, which is a surprise.

phrases.english: A teacher from the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
It is like a flesh-and-blood king
who said to his servants: Come early to my door.
He got up early and found women and men there.
Whom does he praise?
The one who is not used to getting up early, yet got up early.
phrases.notes: That means the women. In the comparison, the earth is like them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 with a parable.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The earth gets special mention because it is like someone who made an unexpected effort, and such a person deserves special praise.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: People do not know what they stand on
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says people see and stand without understanding what they see or what they stand upon.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי says: Woe to the creatures, who see but do not know what they see, who stand but do not know what they stand on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. Here רבי יוסי sets up his next teaching by saying that people do not realize what holds up the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is an opening line that prepares for the explanation in the next step. רבי יוסי first states the problem, that people do not understand. Then he will explain what the earth rests on.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Yosei says:
Woe to the creatures,
who see, and do not know what they see.

phrases.aramaic: עוֹמְדוֹת, וְאֵין יוֹדְעוֹת עַל מָה הֵן עוֹמְדוֹת.
phrases.english: They stand, and do not know what they are standing on.

steps.triggerLanguage: תניא רבי יוסי אומר אוי להם לבריות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about how the world is built, still part of the larger subject of מעשה בראשית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People do not understand what they see or what the world stands on.

steps.title: The chain: what holds up the earth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי lists a chain: earth on pillars, pillars on water, water on mountains, mountains on wind, wind on storm, and storm hangs on God's arm. Each link is proven from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the earth stand on? On pillars, as it says, 'Who shakes the earth from its place, and its pillars tremble.' The pillars stand on water, as it says, 'Who spread the earth over the waters.' The water stands on mountains, as it says, 'The waters stood above the mountains.' The mountains are on the wind, as it says, 'He forms the mountains and creates the wind.' The wind is on a storm, as it says, 'Stormy wind, doing His word.' The storm hangs on the arm of הקדוש ברוך הוא, as it says, 'And underneath are the everlasting arms.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי now explains what people do not know. He gives a step-by-step chain of what holds up the world, with a פסוק for each link.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each layer rests on the one below it, and each is proven from a different פסוק. The chain does not end with something physical. In the end everything hangs on the arm of הקדוש ברוך הוא, so the whole world depends on God.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק as proof)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי, the world rests on a chain of layers: pillars, water, mountains, wind, storm. In the end it all hangs on God's arm.

phrases.aramaic: הָאָרֶץ עַל מָה עוֹמֶדֶת — עַל הָעַמּוּדִים,
phrases.english: What does the earth stand on? On the pillars,
as it is said: 'Who shakes the earth out of its place,
and its pillars tremble.'
The pillars are on the water,
as it is said: 'To Him who spread out the earth over the waters.'
The water is on the mountains,
as it is said: 'The waters stood above the mountains.'
The mountains are on the wind,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי הִנֵּה יוֹצֵר הָרִים וּבוֹרֵא רוּחַ״.
phrases.english: as it is said: 'For behold, He forms the mountains and creates the wind.'
The wind is on a storm,
as it is said: 'Stormy wind, carrying out His word.'

phrases.aramaic: סְעָרָה, תְּלוּיָה בִּזְרוֹעוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא —
phrases.english: The storm hangs on the arm of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it is said: 'And underneath are the everlasting arms.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הארץ על מה עומדת על העמודים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the claim of step 5 by showing what the earth stands on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The earth rests on pillars, which rest on water, then mountains, wind and storm. All of it hangs on the arm of הקדוש ברוך הוא.

steps.title: חכמים: The earth stands on twelve pillars
steps.stepSummary: חכמים say the earth rests on twelve pillars, matching the twelve tribes of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: The earth stands on twelve pillars, as it says, 'He set the borders of the nations according to the number of the children of ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now a different opinion is brought about the pillars. חכמים say there are exactly twelve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ties the world's borders to the number of the children of ישראל. The sons of יעקב were twelve, so the world rests on twelve pillars. This gives a number for the pillars that רבי יוסי mentioned without counting them.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
It stands on twelve pillars,
as it is said: 'He set the borders of the nations
according to the number of the children of Israel.'
phrases.notes: דברים 32:8. The children of ישראל here are the twelve sons of יעקב, which gives twelve pillars.

steps.triggerLanguage: וחכמים אומרים על שנים עשר עמודים עומדת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different view about the pillars mentioned in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The earth stands on twelve pillars.

steps.title: Some say: seven pillars
steps.stepSummary: Another opinion says the earth rests on seven pillars.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: seven pillars, as it says, 'She has carved out her seven pillars.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion is added. It says the number of pillars is seven, based on a פסוק in משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view reads the פסוק about the seven pillars as talking about the pillars of the world. So it disagrees with חכמים about the number.

phrases.english: And some say: seven pillars,
as it is said: 'She has carved out her seven pillars.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 7 about the number of pillars.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The earth stands on seven pillars.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע: One pillar called צדיק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע says the earth rests on one pillar, and its name is צדיק (a righteous person).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע says: On one pillar, and its name is צדיק, as it says, 'But the righteous one is the foundation of the world.'
steps.whatsHappening: The last opinion in the ברייתא says there is only one pillar, and that pillar is the צדיק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier views, which count physical pillars, this view says what holds up the world is the righteous person. The פסוק calls the צדיק the foundation of the world.
steps.whatToRemember: There are four views of what holds up the earth: רבי יוסי's chain, twelve pillars (חכמים), seven pillars (יש אומרים), and one pillar, the צדיק (רבי אלעזר בן שמוע).

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua says:
On one pillar, and its name is 'Righteous One',
as it is said: 'But the righteous one is the foundation of the world.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע אומר על עמוד אחד וצדיק שמו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a final view, different from the counts of twelve and seven in steps 7 and 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The earth stands on one pillar, the צדיק.

steps.title: רב יהודה: There are two רקיעים
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says there are two firmaments, proven from the words 'השמים ושמי השמים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: There are two firmaments, as it says, 'Behold, to ה׳ your God belong the heaven and the heaven of heavens.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic, the heavens above us. רב יהודה starts by saying there are two רקיעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions both 'heaven' and 'the heaven of heavens'. So רב יהודה learns that there is another heaven above our heaven, two in total. In the next step ריש לקיש disagrees and counts seven.

keyTerms.meaning: The heaven of heavens, a heaven above our heaven

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: שְׁנֵי רְקִיעִים הֵן,
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: There are two firmaments,
as it is said: 'Behold, to the Lord your God belong
the heaven and the heaven of heavens.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יהודה שני רקיעים הן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from what is below the earth to what is above it, the heavens.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: there are seven heavens
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says there are seven רקיעים and lists their names.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: There are seven heavens. Their names are וילון, רקיע, שחקים, זבול, מעון, מכון, ערבות.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a different number from רב יהודה: seven heavens, not two. He lists all seven names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a second opinion on the same question רב יהודה answered in step 10. The list also sets up the next steps, where the גמרא explains each heaven one at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: And these are they (introduces a list)
Firmament, a heaven; also the name of the second heaven

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: seven.
phrases.notes: He means seven heavens, answering the same question as רב יהודה's 'two'.

phrases.english: And these are they: Vilon, Rakia, Shechakim,
Zevul, Ma'on, Makhon, Aravot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב יהודה's count of two heavens by giving seven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are seven heavens: וילון, רקיע, שחקים, זבול, מעון, מכון, ערבות.

steps.title: וילון: the curtain that renews Creation daily
steps.stepSummary: וילון holds nothing. It enters in the morning, leaves in the evening, and renews creation every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: וילון has no job of holding anything. It comes in each morning and goes out each evening, and this renews Creation every day, as the פסוק says: 'Who stretches out the heavens like a thin curtain and spreads them like a tent to live in.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the seven heavens, starting with the first, וילון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: וילון means 'curtain'. Unlike the other heavens, nothing sits in it. Its whole role is the daily opening and closing, which renews מעשה בראשית. The פסוק compares the heavens to a curtain being stretched out.

phrases.english: Vilon does not serve any purpose,
phrases.notes: He means nothing is kept inside it, unlike the heavens that come next.

phrases.english: but rather it enters in the morning and goes out in the evening,
and it renews the act of Creation every day,
as it is said: "Who stretches out the heavens like a thin curtain"
"and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the first name on ריש לקיש's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: וילון holds nothing. It enters and leaves daily, renewing Creation.

steps.title: רקיע: where the sun, moon and stars are set
steps.stepSummary: The sun, moon, stars and מזלות are fixed in רקיע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רקיע is the heaven where the sun, moon, stars and constellations are set, as the פסוק says: 'And God placed them in the רקיע of the heavens.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second heaven, רקיע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is simple. The פסוק in בראשית uses the exact word רקיע for where God placed the lights, so that heaven must be the one holding them.

phrases.english: Rakia is the one in which the sun and moon,
stars and constellations are fixed,
as it is said: "And God placed them in the firmament of the heavens."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second heaven on the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sun, moon, stars and constellations are fixed in רקיע.

steps.title: שחקים: where מן is ground for the צדיקים
steps.stepSummary: In שחקים, millstones grind מן for צדיקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: שחקים is the heaven where millstones stand and grind manna for the righteous, as the פסוק says: 'He commanded the skies above and opened the doors of heaven, and He rained manna upon them to eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third heaven, שחקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names שחקים in the same breath as the raining down of מן. From this the גמרא learns that שחקים is where the מן is made.

keyTerms.meaning: Skies; the third heaven (from the root 'to grind')

phrases.english: Shechakim is the one in which millstones stand
and grind manna for the righteous,
as it is said: "And He commanded the skies above"
"and opened the doors of heaven."
"And He rained manna upon them to eat, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 78:23–24. וגו׳ means 'and so on': the פסוק keeps going.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the third heaven on the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שחקים holds the millstones that grind מן for צדיקים.

steps.title: זבול: the heavenly ירושלים, בית המקדש and מזבח
steps.stepSummary: זבול holds a heavenly ירושלים, בית המקדש and מזבח, where מיכאל offers a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: זבול is the heaven where ירושלים and the בית המקדש are, and a מזבח is built there. מיכאל, the great angel-prince, stands and offers a קרבן on it, as the פסוק says: 'I have surely built a house of זבול for You, a place for You to dwell forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the fourth heaven, זבול, and proves it from a פסוק where שלמה calls the בית המקדש a 'house of זבול'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the word זבול to a בית המקדש. So the heaven named זבול holds a heavenly מקדש with an altar, and the angel מיכאל serves there.

phrases.english: Zevul is the one in which Jerusalem and the Temple are,
phrases.notes: He means a heavenly ירושלים and בית המקדש, up in זבול.

phrases.english: and an altar is built there,
and Michael, the great prince,
stands and offers a sacrifice on it,
as it is said: "I have surely built a house of Zevul for You,"
"a place for You to dwell forever."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the fourth heaven on the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זבול holds the heavenly ירושלים, מקדש and מזבח, where מיכאל offers a קרבן.

steps.title: How do we know זבול is called heaven?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that זבול counts as one of the heavens.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that זבול is called 'heaven'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask a question. The last פסוק spoke about a 'house of זבול', but it never called זבול a heaven. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the other heavens, the פסוקים themselves showed a link to the sky (רקיע השמים, דלתי שמים). The פסוק about זבול spoke of a house, so the גמרא wants proof that זבול really belongs on a list of heavens.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it is called heaven?
phrases.notes: 'It' is זבול, which was just described.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the פסוק in step 15 really shows זבול is a heaven.

steps.title: A פסוק pairs heaven with זבול
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in ישעיהו puts שמים and זבול side by side, showing they are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Look down from heaven and see, from Your holy and glorious זבול.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 16 with a פסוק that uses 'heaven' and 'זבול' for the same place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the same thing twice in two ways: 'from heaven' and 'from Your holy זבול'. That shows זבול is a name for a heaven.

phrases.english: As it is written: "Look down from heaven and see"
"from Your holy and glorious Zevul."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק puts 'heaven' and 'זבול' side by side, so זבול is a heaven.

steps.title: מעון: angels who sing only at night
steps.stepSummary: In מעון, groups of מלאכי השרת sing at night and stay silent by day out of respect for ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: מעון is the heaven where groups of מלאכי השרת are. They sing at night and are silent during the day, out of respect for ישראל, as the פסוק says: 'By day ה׳ commands His kindness, and at night His song is with me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the fifth heaven, מעון, home of the singing angels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angels only sing at night so that the day belongs to the praise of ישראל. The פסוק is read this way: by day ה׳ shows kindness to ישראל, and only 'at night' is His (the angels') song with Him.

phrases.aramaic: מָעוֹן — שֶׁבּוֹ כִּיתּוֹת שֶׁל מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת,
phrases.english: Ma'on is the one in which there are groups of ministering angels,
who sing song at night
and are silent by day,
because of the honor of Israel,
as it is said: "By day ה׳ commands His kindness,"
"and at night His song is with me."

steps.triggerLanguage: מָעוֹן — שֶׁבּוֹ כִּיתּוֹת שֶׁל מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the fifth heaven on the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In מעון, angels sing at night and stay silent by day out of respect for ישראל.

steps.title: Learning Torah at night brings kindness by day
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that whoever learns תורה at night gets a 'thread of חסד' from ה׳ during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Whoever learns תורה at night, הקדוש ברוך הוא draws a thread of kindness over him during the day, as it says: 'By day ה׳ commands His kindness.' Why does ה׳ command His kindness by day? Because 'at night His song is with me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps away from the list of heavens. Using the same פסוק just quoted, ריש לקיש teaches about learning תורה at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'His song at night' is read as the song of תורה learned at night. The two halves of the פסוק are linked as cause and effect: night learning causes daytime חסד.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, blessed be He

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source for the special value of learning תורה at night.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Anyone who toils in Torah at night,
the Holy One, blessed be He, draws over him
a thread of kindness by day,
as it is said: "By day ה׳ commands His kindness."
And what is the reason that "By day ה׳ commands His kindness"?
Because "at night His song is with me."
phrases.notes: Here 'His song' means the song of תורה that a person learns at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כׇּל הָעוֹסֵק בְּתוֹרָה בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reuses the פסוק from step 18 for a new teaching about learning תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning תורה at night brings a thread of ה׳'s חסד during the day.

steps.title: Second version: this world is night, the next world is day
steps.stepSummary: Some report ריש לקיש's teaching differently: learning תורה in this world, which is like night, earns חסד in עולם הבא, which is like day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say ריש לקיש said: Whoever learns תורה in עולם הזה, which is like night, הקדוש ברוך הוא draws a thread of kindness over him in עולם הבא, which is like day, as it says: 'By day ה׳ commands His kindness, and at night His song is with me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of ריש לקיש's teaching. In this version, 'night' and 'day' are read as pictures, not as actual times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, 'night' and 'day' were real hours. Here, 'night' stands for עולם הזה and 'day' for עולם הבא. Same פסוק, same structure, but the reward moves to the next world.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש listed seven heavens and explained five of them here. The פסוק about מעון led to his teaching that learning תורה at 'night' earns ה׳'s חסד by 'day'. The two versions differ on whether night and day mean real times or this world and the next.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument against the first version. It is the same teaching from the same speaker, reported in a different way.

phrases.english: And some say, Reish Lakish said:
Anyone who toils in Torah in this world,
which is like night,

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מוֹשֵׁךְ עָלָיו חוּט שֶׁל חֶסֶד
phrases.english: the Holy One, blessed be He, draws over him a thread of kindness
in the World to Come, which is like day,
as it is said: "By day ה׳ commands His kindness,"
"and at night His song is with me."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the teaching in step 19, reading night and day as this world and the next.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning תורה in עולם הזה ('night') earns a thread of חסד in עולם הבא ('day').

steps.title: Pausing from Torah for idle talk is punished with broom-tree coals
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי teaches that someone who stops learning תורה to chat about pointless things is fed burning coals of the broom tree, based on a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: Anyone who stops learning תורה and turns to idle chatter will be fed coals of the broom tree, as it says: 'They pluck saltwort with wormwood, and the roots of the broom tree are their food.'
steps.whatsHappening: Still on the topic of learning תורה (from the last steps), רבי לוי adds a warning about stopping in the middle of learning to chat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 19-20 promised reward for learning תורה, and this step shows the opposite side, the punishment for interrupting it. The proof is a wordplay on the פסוק: 'plucking' means cutting yourself off, and 'שיח' sounds like idle talk.

keyTerms.meaning: coals of the broom tree, which burn very long and hot
those who pluck or cut off

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:
Anyone who stops from words of Torah
and busies himself with idle conversation
is fed coals of the broom tree,
as it says: 'They pluck saltwort with wormwood,
phrases.notes: איוב 30:4. מלוח sounds like לוחות, the Torah's tablets, and שיח sounds like chatter: people who cut themselves off from Torah to chat.

phrases.english: and the roots of the broom tree are their food.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי כׇּל הַפּוֹסֵק מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the punishment for interrupting תורה study, balancing the reward described in steps 19-20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Interrupting תורה for idle talk brings the punishment of broom-tree coals.

steps.title: Source that מעון counts as heaven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that מעון is called שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that it is called 'heaven'?
steps.whatsHappening: Following its usual pattern, the גמרא asks for a source that מעון is one of the heavens. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each heaven in the list has to be shown to really be called שמים in תנ״ך. The same question was asked about זבול in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: and from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it is called heaven?
phrases.notes: "It" means מעון, the heaven described back in step 18.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to מעון, after the side teachings about תורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that מעון is called שמים.

steps.title: A פסוק links מעון with heaven
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'Look down from Your holy מעון, from heaven' treats מעון and שמים as the same place.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Look down from Your holy dwelling (מעון), from heaven.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק that puts מעון right next to שמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק explains 'from Your holy מעון' with 'from heaven', it shows that מעון is a name for one of the heavens.

phrases.english: As it says: 'Look down from Your holy dwelling,
from heaven.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in דברים places מעון side by side with שמים.

steps.title: מכון holds the storehouses of snow, hail and harmful weather
steps.stepSummary: The next heaven, מכון, contains storehouses of snow and hail, harmful dew, drops, storms and mist, all behind doors of fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: מכון is where the storehouses of snow and hail are, the upper room of harmful dews, the upper room of drops, the room of storm and tempest, and the cave of mist. Their doors are fire. As it says: 'ה׳ will open for you His good storehouse.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the sixth heaven, מכון, and lists what is kept there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of these are damaging kinds of weather. The proof is that the פסוק calls one storehouse 'good', which suggests there are also storehouses of bad things.

keyTerms.meaning: the sixth heaven, literally 'a set place'

phrases.english: מכון is where there are storehouses of snow
and storehouses of hail,
and the upper room of harmful dews,
and the upper room of drops,
and the room of storm [and tempest],
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording, but not every version has it.

phrases.english: and the cave of mist.
And their doors are fire.
As it says: 'ה׳ will open for you
His good storehouse.'
phrases.notes: דברים 28:12. Calling it the 'good' storehouse hints that there are bad storehouses too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After מעון, the list continues with the next heaven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מכון contains the storehouses of harmful weather, sealed with doors of fire.

steps.title: But these things are on earth, not in heaven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: a פסוק in תהלים lists fire, hail, snow, mist and storm wind as praising ה׳ 'from the earth'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these in the heaven? These are on the earth! As it is written: 'Praise ה׳ from the earth, sea monsters and all depths, fire and hail, snow and mist, stormy wind that does His word.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the list in step 24 by pointing to a פסוק that places these same things on earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 put snow, hail, mist and storm in מכון. Yet the פסוק names these exact items among the things that praise ה׳ 'from the earth'. That looks like a direct contradiction.

phrases.english: Are these things in the heaven?
These are on the earth!
As it is written: 'Praise ה׳ from the earth,
sea monsters and all depths,
fire and hail, snow and mist,
stormy wind that does His word.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי בִּרְקִיעָא אִיתַנְהוּ הָנֵי בְּאַרְעָא אִיתַנְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the description of מכון in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that snow, hail, mist and storm are stored in מכון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק explicitly lists these same items as being 'from the earth'.

steps.title: דוד prayed and they were brought down to earth
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב answers that they were once in heaven, but דוד asked ה׳ to bring them down, since evil things should not live near ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: דוד asked for mercy about them, and He brought them down to earth. דוד said before Him: רבונו של עולם, 'You are not a God who wants wickedness; evil does not dwell with You.' You are righteous, ה׳, so evil should not dwell near You.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: both are true, at different times. The harmful weather started in heaven and was later moved down to earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 describes where they were originally stored, and the פסוק in תהלים describes where they are now. דוד argued from a פסוק that harmful things do not belong next to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: evil will not dwell with You

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
David asked for mercy about them,
and He brought them down to earth.
He said before Him: Master of the world,
'You are not a God who wants wickedness;
evil does not dwell with You.'
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out. The פסוק itself reads לא יגורך רע.

phrases.english: You are righteous, ה׳,
so evil should not dwell in Your dwelling place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב דָּוִד בִּיקֵּשׁ עֲלֵיהֶם רַחֲמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Time-based split: originally in heaven, later moved to earth.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק in תהלים seemed to show that these things were never in heaven.
steps.terutzMaskana: They were in מכון at first, and דוד's prayer brought them down to earth.
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps the description of מכון intact while explaining why harmful weather is found on earth today.

steps.title: Source that מכון counts as heaven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that מכון is called שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that it is called 'heaven'?
steps.whatsHappening: Once again the גמרא asks for a source, this time showing that מכון is one of the heavens. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same standard question asked for every heaven. Here it is applied to מכון.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it is called 'heaven'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the description of מכון, after the challenge and answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that מכון is called שמים.

steps.title: A פסוק links מכון with heaven
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'You will hear in heaven, the מכון of Your dwelling' shows that מכון is a heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And You will hear in heaven, the place (מכון) of Your dwelling.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק from שלמה's prayer that calls heaven 'מכון'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק explains 'heaven' with 'מכון of Your dwelling', so the two are the same place.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And You will hear in heaven,
the place of Your dwelling.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב וְאַתָּה תִּשְׁמַע הַשָּׁמַיִם מְכוֹן שִׁבְתֶּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in מלכים calls heaven 'מכון of Your dwelling'.

steps.title: What is found in ערבות, the highest heaven
steps.stepSummary: ערבות holds צדק, משפט and צדקה, the treasuries of life, peace and blessing, the souls of צדיקים, souls not yet created, and the dew for תחיית המתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: ערבות is where there are צדק, משפט and צדקה; the treasuries of life, peace and blessing; the souls of the צדיקים; the spirits and souls that will be created in the future; and the dew with which הקדוש ברוך הוא will bring the dead back to life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the seventh and highest heaven, ערבות, and lists everything stored there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מכון held harmful things, while ערבות holds only the most precious ones: moral values, blessings and souls. It also holds the dew that will be used to revive the dead.

keyTerms.meaning: to bring the dead back to life

phrases.english: ערבות is where there are righteousness, justice and charity,
the treasuries of life and the treasuries of peace
and the treasuries of blessing,
and the souls of the righteous,
and the spirits and souls that will be created in the future,
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording, which makes the word fit 'spirits and souls'.

phrases.english: and the dew with which the Holy One, Blessed be He, will in the future
bring the dead back to life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from מכון to the last heaven in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ערבות holds the highest spiritual treasures, souls, and the dew of תחיית המתים.

steps.title: Sources for the treasures of ערבות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins proving the items of ערבות from פסוקים: צדק and משפט, צדקה, life, peace and blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Righteousness and justice, as it is written: 'Righteousness and justice are the base of Your throne.' Charity, as it is written: 'He wore righteousness like armor.' The treasuries of life, as it is written: 'For with You is the source of life.' The treasuries of peace, as it is written: 'And he called Him ה׳ of peace.' The treasuries of blessing, as it is written: 'He will receive a blessing from ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through the list from step 29 one item at a time and brings a פסוק for each. Each פסוק shows that the item is right next to ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק links the item to ה׳'s throne, His clothing, or His presence, so it must be in the highest heaven. The proofs for the remaining items (souls and the dew) come in the next step.

phrases.english: Righteousness and justice, as it is written:
'Righteousness and justice are the base of Your throne.'
Charity, as it is written:
'He wore righteousness like armor.'
The treasuries of life, as it is written:
'For with You is the source of life.'
And the treasuries of peace, as it is written:
'And he called Him ה׳ of peace.'
phrases.notes: שופטים 6:24. Peace is used as ה׳'s name, so it is close to Him.

phrases.english: And the treasuries of blessing, as it is written:
'He will receive a blessing from ה׳.'

steps.triggerLanguage: צֶדֶק וּמִשְׁפָּט דִּכְתִיב צֶדֶק וּמִשְׁפָּט מְכוֹן כִּסְאֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports each item listed in step 29 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That צדק, משפט, צדקה, life, peace and blessing are stored in ערבות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: פסוקים from תהלים, ישעיהו and שופטים linking each item to ה׳ Himself.

steps.title: Proofs for the souls and the dew stored in ערבות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings פסוקים showing that ערבות holds the souls of צדיקים, the souls not yet created, and the dew for תחיית המתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The souls of the righteous are there, as it says: 'The soul of my master shall be bound in the bundle of life with ה׳ your God.' Spirits and souls not yet created are there, as it says: 'For the spirit that wraps itself is from before Me, and the souls that I have made.' The dew that ה׳ will use to bring the dead back to life is there, as it says: 'A generous rain You will pour down, God...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing its list of proofs from step 30, now proving the last three items it said are stored in ערבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item gets its own פסוק. The souls of צדיקים are 'bound up with ה׳', so they are close to Him. New souls come 'from before Me', and the 'generous rain' is read as the special dew ה׳ keeps for תחיית המתים.

keyTerms.meaning: The bundle of life, where the souls of the righteous are kept
Bringing the dead back to life

steps.whatToRemember: Every item stored in ערבות has now been backed up by a פסוק.

phrases.english: The souls of the righteous are there —
as it is written: "And the soul of my master shall be bound
in the bundle of life with ה׳ your God."
Spirits and souls that are going to be created are there —
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording, making the word plural to match 'spirits and souls'.

phrases.english: as it is written: "For the spirit that wraps itself is from before Me,
and the souls that I have made."
And the dew that the Holy One, Blessed be He, will in the future
use to bring the dead back to life is there —
as it is written: "A generous rain You will pour down, God;
when Your inheritance was weary, You established it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of proofs that step 30 began.
steps.raayaObject: That the souls of צדיקים, future souls, and the resurrection dew are in ערבות

steps.title: The heavenly beings in ערבות and ה׳ above them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists the heavenly beings and the כסא הכבוד in ערבות, and says ה׳ dwells above them there, proven by 'סולו לרוכב בערבות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are the אופנים, the שרפים, the holy חיות, the ministering angels, and the Throne of Glory. The King, the living, lofty and exalted God, dwells above them in ערבות, as it says: 'Extol Him who rides upon ערבות, whose name is יה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds more to the description of ערבות: the angels and the כסא הכבוד are there, and ה׳ dwells above them all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'Him who rides upon ערבות' shows that ה׳ is pictured as being in ערבות. This sets up the next question: how do we know ערבות counts as a 'heaven' at all?

keyTerms.meaning: The holy living creatures, a type of angel

phrases.english: There are the אופנים, the שרפים, and the holy חיות,
and the ministering angels, and the Throne of Glory.
The King, the living, lofty and exalted God,
dwells above them in ערבות,
as it is said: "Extol Him who rides upon ערבות, whose name is יה."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues describing what is in ערבות, now turning to the angels and ה׳ Himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The angels and the כסא הכבוד are in ערבות, and ה׳ dwells above them there.

steps.title: How do we know ערבות is called heaven?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that ערבות is called שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that ערבות is called 'heaven'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the next step: where does the תורה call ערבות a 'heaven'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question the גמרא asked about מכון in step 27. ערבות is being counted as one of the seven heavens, so the גמרא wants proof that it really is a 'heaven'.

phrases.english: And how do we know that it is called "heaven"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source behind calling ערבות a heaven, mentioned in step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that ערבות is called שמים.

steps.title: Learning it from the word 'rides' in both places
steps.stepSummary: A גזירה שוה from the word 'rides': ה׳ 'rides upon ערבות' and 'rides the heavens', so ערבות is the heavens.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from 'riding' and 'riding'. Here it says: 'Extol Him who rides upon ערבות', and there it says: 'Who rides the heavens to help you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by matching the same word, 'rides', in two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק says ה׳ rides upon ערבות, and another says He rides upon שמים. Since the same word is used, the two places are treated as the same, so ערבות is called שמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning from the same word appearing in two places

phrases.english: It is learned from "riding" and "riding."
It is written here: "Extol Him who rides upon ערבות,"
and it is written there: "Who rides the heavens to help you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'rides' links ערבות with שמים, so ערבות is called heaven.

steps.title: Darkness, cloud and fog surround ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says darkness, cloud and fog surround ה׳, based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And darkness, cloud and fog surround Him, as it says: 'He made darkness His hiding place, His shelter all around Him: darkness of waters, thick clouds of the skies.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more detail about ערבות‎: ה׳ is surrounded by darkness, cloud and fog.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes darkness as ה׳'s 'hiding place' and 'shelter all around Him'. This statement is about to be challenged in the next step.

phrases.english: And darkness, cloud and fog surround Him —
as it is said: "He made darkness His hiding place,
His shelter all around Him:
darkness of waters, thick clouds of the skies."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the description of ה׳'s place in ערבות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Darkness, cloud and fog surround ה׳.

steps.title: But light dwells with ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: how can there be darkness before ה׳, when a פסוק in דניאל says light dwells with Him?
steps.simpleTranslation: But is there darkness before Heaven? Doesn't it say: 'He reveals the deep and hidden things, He knows what is in the darkness, and the light dwells with Him'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last statement by quoting a פסוק that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 35 said darkness surrounds ה׳. But the פסוק in דניאל says light dwells with Him, which seems to mean no darkness is there. The two פסוקים seem to clash.

phrases.english: But is there darkness before Heaven?
phrases.notes: 'Heaven' here is a respectful way of saying ה׳.

phrases.english: But isn't it written: "He reveals the deep and hidden things,
He knows what is in the darkness,
and the light dwells with Him!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the statement of step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement that darkness surrounds ה׳.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק says light dwells with ה׳, which seems to leave no room for darkness near Him.

steps.title: The answer begins: it is not difficult
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer, saying the two פסוקים do not really clash, and begins to explain which פסוק refers to what.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer: it says there is no real problem and starts to explain that each פסוק talks about something different. The full answer continues on the next amud.
